title: Products That Have Never Been Ordered
description:
Find all products that have never appeared in any order using a NOT EXISTS subquery.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`

**Table: order_items** — `id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `quantity`

Output columns: `name`, `category`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A','Electronics'),(2,'Widget B','Electronics'),(3,'Shirt X','Clothing'),(4,'Shirt Y','Clothing'),(5,'Book 1','Books'),(6,'Book 2','Books'),(7,'Gadget Z','Electronics'),(8,'Pants W','Clothing'); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INT, order_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1001,1,2),(2,1001,3,1),(3,1002,2,3),(4,1002,5,1),(5,1003,4,2),(6,1003,1,1);
solution_sql: SELECT name, category FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.id) ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 8 products; products 1,2,3,4,5 are ordered; products 6 (Book 2), 7 (Gadget Z), 8 (Pants W) are never ordered — 3 rows

hints: NOT EXISTS returns TRUE when the subquery finds no matching rows — the complement of EXISTS.
This is equivalent to a LEFT JOIN ... WHERE order_items.product_id IS NULL, but NOT EXISTS is often clearer in intent.
explanation: NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items WHERE product_id = p.id) is TRUE when no order item references that product. Products 6 (Book 2), 7 (Gadget Z), and 8 (Pants W) have no matching rows in order_items, so they are returned. This is a common pattern for finding orphan or unused records.
